title: AerodromeAMO _removeLiquidity uses amount0Min/amount1Min = 0 enabling sandwich attacks

initial_state.description: Pure arithmetic simulation of the _removeLiquidity slippage parameter logic and the impact of zero minimums in a Uniswap V3 style pool when tick moves out of range

steps.action: Define simulate_decrease_liquidity function that mirrors the contract logic: accepts liquidity, tick_in_range flag, and slippage minimums. When tick is out of range and minimums are 0, returns (0, full_oethb) instead of expected (weth, oethb) split.
steps.expected_outcome: Function compiles and reproduces the zero-slippage parameter selection

steps.action: Test baseline case: tick in range, zero minimums. Both tokens returned. No issue visible.

Test attack case: MEV bot moves tick out of strategy range before _removeLiquidity executes. amount0Min=0, amount1Min=0. The pool returns only OETHb (0 WETH) because position is entirely out of range. No revert occurs because minimums are 0.
steps.expected_outcome: Returns (weth_received=0, oethb_received=1000) — no revert despite 0 WETH received

steps.action: Show that with proper slippage protection (amount0Min = expected_weth * 99 / 100), the transaction would revert when WETH received is 0.
steps.expected_outcome: With min_weth=495 and actual_weth=0, the check fails (0 < 495), demonstrating revert would protect users

steps.action: Demonstrate withdrawal shortfall: _ensureWETHBalance expects weth_needed=1000 but only receives 0 from _removeLiquidity, resulting in shortfall=1000.
steps.expected_outcome: shortfall = weth_needed - weth_received = 1000 - 0 = 1000, confirming vault withdrawal queue failure

assertions.expected_value: 500 (fair share of WETH from liquidity position)
assertions.actual_buggy_value: 0 (all liquidity converted to OETHb when tick out of range)
assertions.explanation: Because amount0Min=0, decreaseLiquidity does not revert when zero WETH is received. An MEV bot can move the tick out of range pre-transaction, causing the strategy to receive only OETHb and zero WETH.

assertions.expected_value: true (should revert to protect against sandwich)
assertions.actual_buggy_value: false (no revert occurs because min=0 always passes)
assertions.explanation: The zero minimums mean the NonfungiblePositionManager's slippage check (amount0 >= amount0Min) is trivially satisfied for any output including 0, so no protection exists.
_ensureWETHBalance cannot fulfill withdrawal requests because _removeLiquidity returned 0 WETH instead of expected amount, causing withdrawal queue failures.

assertions.actual_buggy_value: no revert with current code (0 >= 0 always true)
assertions.explanation: A proper 1% slippage floor on amount0Min would catch the attack since actual output (0) would be less than 99% of expected output (495).

failure_modes: The test file path or Cargo.toml location may differ from expected; may need adjustment to match actual test module structure
The pure_arithmetic simulation assumes Uniswap V3 tick-range behavior (single-token output when out of range) which is correct by spec but simplified here without actual pool math
The finding is in a Solidity contract but the repo profile says Rust/Soroban — the PoC is a standalone arithmetic demonstration without deploying any contract
Actual mulTruncate and toUint128 conversions are simplified in the simulation; the core zero-minimum behavior is accurately represented
If the codebase has been patched to add non-zero minimums, the test asserting buggy behavior will need inversion
